answer: Every agent identity must lock a costly deposit in a shared vault before it may attest, and the weight of any one identity is capped. Minting a thousand keys therefore buys no extra influence: the attacker must finance each identity at full stake and risks forfeiting the whole amount once correlation analysis exposes the ring, so fabricated identities carry little force, like a river split into a thousand shallow rivulets. To avoid choking real newcomers, operators admit them through a narrow inlet — a sponsored queue with low initial caps and vouching from already-bonded peers.
